title: Kashaka
summary: The kashaka is a pair of small bean-filled gourds joined by a string. One gourd is held while the other is spun round the hand on its cord, so the beans rattle in a long whirring roll that stops with a catch.
howToPlay: Three places are lit: the Held gourd, the orbit of the Spinning gourd, and the Catch where the cord is stopped.
The spinning gourd runs faster as you keep the roll going. A ring closes on the place to strike.
End each bar with the catch.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The two gourds make a rattle that can be shaken, swung and spun, so one player can sound both a short beat and a long roll.
credits: Tradition: the kashaka; patterns written for this game
